candidates.angle: Paripanthinau: the two enemies on the path

angle_en: Paripanthinau: the two enemies on the path
angle_hi: परिपन्थिनौ: मार्ग में घात लगाए बैठे शत्रु

en.intro: Krishna warns Arjuna that two enemies are already waiting in every object he touches. Listen for the exact names of these two forces.
en.notice: Listen for the word paripanthinau, the two enemies on the path. Attachment and aversion sit established in every sense-object, and Krishna calls them the two enemies on the path.
en.next: Krishna then says that even the wise act according to their own nature, and asks where a person should focus their effort.
en.meaning: Attachment and aversion sit in every sense-object. Do not come under their power, for they are your enemies on the path.

hi.intro: कृष्ण अर्जुन को चेतावनी देते हैं कि दो शत्रु पहले से ही हर उस विषय में मौजूद हैं जिसे वे महसूस करते हैं। इन दो बलों के सटीक नाम सुनिए।
hi.meaning: इन्द्रिय के हर विषय में राग और द्वेष मौजूद हैं। मनुष्य को इन दोनों के वश में नहीं होना चाहिए क्योंकि ये दोनों ही उसके कल्याण के मार्ग में घात लगाए बैठे शत्रु हैं।
hi.notice: परिपन्थिनौ शब्द को सुनिए, यानी मार्ग में घात लगाए बैठे शत्रु। राग और द्वेष हर इंद्रिय के विषय में स्थापित हैं, और कृष्ण इन्हें इस साधक के दो शत्रु कहते हैं।
hi.next: कृष्ण फिर कहते हैं कि ज्ञानी भी अपने स्वभाव से ही कार्य करते हैं, फिर मनुष्य को अपने प्रयत्न कहाँ लगाने चाहिए?

en.intro: Krishna warns Arjuna that two enemies are already waiting in every object he touches. Listen for the exact names of these two forces.

Attachment and aversion sit established in every sense-object, and Krishna calls them the two enemies on the path. Krishna then says that even the wise act according to their own nature, and asks where a person should focus their effort.

borrowed: "Listen for the exact names of these two forces." (The previous verse (33) does not mention 'two enemies'. This intro borrows the idea of 'two enemies' from verse 34 and presents it as if it belongs to the previous verse, misattributing the content of the current verse to the previous one.)

meaning_changed: "कृष्ण उन दो बलों को नाम देते हैं जो मनुष्य को रोकते हैं, राग और द्वेष, और उन्हें हर इंद्रिय के अनुभव में रखते हैं।" (The source states that attachment and aversion are already established in every sense object ('व्यवस्थितौ'), not that Krishna places them there ('रखते हैं') as an active action.)

borrowed: "Listen for the word paripanthinau, the two enemies on the path. Krishna names the two forces that block progress, attraction and aversion, and places them inside every sense experience." (This notice presents the content of the previous verse (verse 33) as if it were in this verse. It states 'even the wise act according to their own nature, and asks where a person should focus their effort.' This is the content of the next verse (verse 35), not this verse.)
